name: Ojai
tagline: A rail-trail, a gravel mountain and one long climb
best_months: November to May for the dirt. Bikepacking.com gives that window for the Ojai Rim Loop and calls February and March best, when it's cooler and the creeks run. Pathless Pedaled says to ride Sulphur Mountain in the cooler months. Inland Ojai is hot in summer, so start early then.
summary: Ojai is a small town in a valley in Ventura County with one car-free path, one gravel mountain and one long highway climb. The Ojai Valley Trail runs 9.3 paved miles from Bryant Street to Foster Park and on to Ventura, about 15 miles in all. Sulphur Mountain Road is 9 miles of gated dirt, and Highway 33 climbs 10.8 miles into Los Padres National Forest. Center Ride Out, the Los Angeles LGBT Center's three-day ride, camps in Ojai on April 23–25, 2027. There's no airport and no train, so plan on a car to get here. Santa Barbara is the closest airport, about 34 miles west in a straight line.
about: Ojai sits in a valley in Ventura County at 745 feet: 7,637 people at the 2020 census, in 4.4 square miles. This guide covers the town and the valley around it. That's Meiners Oaks and the west end toward Lake Casitas. Mira Monte, Oak View and Casitas Springs down the bike path. Upper Ojai over the hill to the east. Ventura, about 12 miles south, is a different town. It's here only for the shops that are open when Ojai's is shut and the clubs that ride up the path.

It's written for two readers. The first is the Center Ride Out rider. The ride reaches Ojai on Friday, April 23, 2027. Riders can stay in camp or ride an out-and-back on Saturday. They roll for Los Angeles by 7:00 am on Sunday. The Center has not published where the camp is. Saturday is the day for coffee, a shop and a short ride. The second reader is whoever drives up to meet them and needs a room. Or anyone who comes with a bike on another weekend.

Ojai is one of everything. One bike shop, The Mob Shop, downtown and closed Tuesday and Wednesday. One coffee place open at 6 every day, Ojai Coffee Roasters. We found no recurring group ride that starts in the valley. The rides that reach it come up the path from Ventura. Dinner ends early: most kitchens close by 8 or 9.
riding: Start with the Ojai Valley Trail. It's a paved rail-trail, car-free, 9.3 miles from Bryant Street in Ojai down to Foster Park. There the Ventura River Trail carries on to the coast, about 15 miles in all. It drops gently the whole way, so the climb is on the way home: about 500 feet from Foster Park, 800 to 1,000 from Ventura. Weekends are crowded and the pavement has root bumps.

The short road climb is the Upper Ojai Summit: 6.5 miles and 781 feet east out of town on a two-lane road with narrow shoulders. The long one is Highway 33 north: 10.8 miles and 2,625 feet at 4.6 percent. It goes through the three Wheeler Gorge tunnels, and there's no water you can count on. Caltrans is rebuilding those tunnels and expects to finish in winter 2026/2027, so check State Route 33 before you go. The long road day is the Lake Casitas loop, 48 miles out Highway 150 to the coast and home up the path.

The gravel is Sulphur Mountain Road: about 9 miles and 2,100 feet of gated ranch road. Cattle on it, no cars, no water and little shade. Ride it as a 30-mile loop from town. The Ojai Rim Loop is the two-day version, 67 miles and 10,277 feet. Both are for the cooler months.
getting_there: Drive. Ojai has no airport and no train. Santa Barbara Airport (SBA) is the closest with airlines, about 34 miles west in a straight line. Hollywood Burbank is about 54 and Los Angeles International about 59 southeast. The drive is longer than each number. From the south or the coast, take the 101 to Ventura and Highway 33 north, 14 miles to town. Route 150 over Casitas Pass also comes in from the 101. The Ojai Valley Inn's directions page says to skip it in rain, at night or if you don't know the road (Nov 2026). Without a car: Gold Coast Transit Route 16 links the Ventura Transit Center with downtown Ojai. Every bus has a front rack for three built bikes, free. The nearest train is the Pacific Surfliner in Ventura, where a full-size bike rides free with a reserved bike space. Ventura is the bottom of the bike path, about 15 miles below Ojai.

routes.name: Ojai Valley Trail
routes.surface: Paved bike path on an old rail line. Some stretches are bumpy and cracked from tree roots and flooding. A wood-chip horse path runs beside it behind a fence.
routes.description: The car-free path down the valley. TrailLink lists it as a 9.3-mile rail-trail from Bryant Street in Ojai to Foster Park (37 Casitas Vista Rd). There it meets the Ventura River Trail and keeps going to the coast. Ojai to Ventura is about 15 miles one way, gently downhill, so the climb is on the way home. That's about 500 feet from Foster Park back up to Ojai, 800 to 1,000 from Ventura. Ride out as far as you like and turn around. The miles and feet here are one way, Ojai to Foster Park. Blue Iguana Inn sits beside the path, and Ojai Valley Brewery is on Bryant Street, the street the Ojai end is on.
routes.water: Carry it. Restrooms at Libbey Park in Ojai and at Foster Park. No fountain is named on the trail pages. Shops and gas stations along the route will refill a bottle (Two Wheeled Wanderer, Jan 2024).
routes.hazards: It crosses streets in Ojai, crosses Highway 33 near Ojai, and passes the busy Highway 150 / Baldwin Road intersection. It gets crowded on weekends with walkers and e-bikes; bring a bell. Root bumps and cracks in the pavement. Ojai gets hot; go early in summer.

routes.name: Upper Ojai Summit climb

start.name: East Ojai Avenue, east edge of town

routes.description: The short climb east out of town to Upper Ojai. The segment is 6.5 miles and 781 feet at a 2.3% average, 7.5% at its steepest, from 663 feet to 1,421. It starts about a mile and a half east of the center of town. Short enough for a Saturday morning: up, turn around, back for coffee. It's graded moderate, not easy. You share a two-lane road with cars, and it isn't a quiet one.
routes.hazards: A winding two-lane road with narrow shoulders between Ojai and Santa Paula (Komoot's route notes). You share the lane with cars the whole way up and down.

routes.name: Sulphur Mountain Road loop
routes.surface: Mixed: paved path, a short stretch of Highway 33, about 9 miles of gated dirt fire road, then paved road back. The dirt is rough in places from cattle and horses, muddy after rain and bumpy once it dries.

start.name: Downtown Ojai (street parking a few blocks off Ojai Avenue)

routes.description: Where the gravel bikes go. Down the Ojai Valley Trail, a short stretch on Highway 33, then up Sulphur Mountain Road. It's a gated ranch road, closed to cars. About 9 miles and 2,100 feet at a 5% average (12% at its steepest), from about 400 feet to 2,300. It comes out on pavement in Upper Ojai and drops back to town on a switchbacked road. Bring a gravel bike with wide tires, not a road bike. Ride it in the cooler months. The Channel Islands Bicycle Club posted a version of this loop from Ventura for April 2, 2026.
routes.hazards: Cattle on the road, sometimes standing in the middle of it; close the gates behind you. No water and little shade on the climb, so carry plenty. Hoof ruts make the dirt rough, and it is slick mud after rain. The return is a switchbacked descent on a two-lane road. The fire road is busy on weekends.

routes.name: Highway 33 climb, Matilija to the top

start.name: Highway 33 (Maricopa Highway) north of Ojai, where the climb starts

routes.description: The climb. Highway 33 leaves the valley, runs through Wheeler Gorge and its three tunnels, and keeps going up into Los Padres National Forest. The segment is 10.8 miles and 2,625 feet at a 4.6% average, from 943 feet to 3,568. The miles and feet are one way, and the start is about 4 miles from the center of town. From Ojai and back it's a much bigger day than the numbers say. Turn around at the top and come down the way you went up. Ojai Deer Lodge is on the same road, Maricopa Highway.
routes.water: None you can count on. The Forest Service says there is no potable water on the byway. A 2015 ride report says Wheeler Gorge Campground has no running water and that bottled water was sold at the visitor center there. That's old, so don't plan on it. Fill up in Ojai.
routes.hazards: Three tunnels in Wheeler Gorge; a 2015 ride report says the first one curves and is disorienting inside. Caltrans is rebuilding the three tunnels (post miles 18.2 to 19.0). It shut the road to everyone for 55 hours on Aug 28 to 31, 2026, and expects to finish in winter 2026/2027 (Caltrans release, Aug 12, 2026). Check Caltrans for State Route 33 before you go. Rocks and gravel fall onto the road, which matters most on the way down. The road draws motorcycle groups and car clubs. Spotty or no cell service in the gorge (2015 report). No services. Wind on the descent. Los Padres National Forest listed fire danger as Very High on Nov 15, 2026.

routes.name: Lake Casitas loop
routes.surface: Paved. About 27 miles of it is bike path, about 16 is state highway.

start.name: Ojai (the route page names the town, not a spot)

routes.description: The long road day from town. West on Highway 150 past Lake Casitas, down to the coast at Mussel Shoals, south along the shore past Faria County Park to Ventura, then home up the bike path. 48 miles and about 2,800 feet, topping out near 1,100 feet. More than half of it is car-free path. The climbing on the path comes last.
routes.water: Faria County Park on the coast has restrooms and water (Komoot's notes on the neighboring loop). Nothing else is named.
routes.hazards: Highway 150 is busy at commute times; about 16 miles of the loop is on state highway. The bike path is crowded on weekends and has root bumps and cracks. Inland it is hot in summer; start early.

routes.name: Ojai Rim Loop
routes.surface: Mixed: 78% unpaved, 17% singletrack, the rest paved.

start.name: Sulphur Mountain Road trailhead, between Casitas Springs and Oak View

routes.description: A two-day bikepacking loop around the rim of the valley: up Sulphur Mountain Road, up Sisar Road to Nordhoff Ridge, and back down through Meiners Oaks. The high point is 6,700 feet, on an optional out-and-back to Hines Peak. 67 miles and 10,277 feet, 28 miles and 6,676 feet of it on day one. Bikepacking.com says you can leave a car overnight at the trailhead. Rideable November through May; February and March are best, when it is cooler and the creeks run. Not a ride for the day after an 80-mile day.
routes.water: Stagecoach Store and Summit Drive-In on Highway 150, and a spigot at the Ventura County fire station just west of the drive-in. Sisar Creek usually runs at the bottom of the Sisar Road climb. Nothing sure after that until Meiners Oaks; carry 4 to 6 liters when it is dry.
routes.hazards: Long, dry, exposed climbs; heat is the main danger. Rattlesnakes, black bears and mountain lions. No camping on Sulphur Mountain Road. Fires only in the fire rings at the Nordhoff Ridge Road campsites; check Los Padres fire restrictions first (fire danger was listed Very High on Nov 15, 2026).

coffee.name: Ojai Coffee Roasters
coffee.note: Downtown, on Ojai Avenue. Opens at 6 every day, Saturday and Sunday included, so it's the one that's open before a 7:00 roll-out. The kitchen runs 9 to 2, so before that it's coffee, not breakfast. Its site says nothing about bike parking or outdoor tables.
coffee.hours_hint: 6 a.m. daily; closes 5 p.m. Monday to Thursday, 6 p.m. Friday to Sunday; kitchen 9 to 2

coffee.name: Coffee Connection
coffee.address: 311 East El Roblar Drive, Ojai, CA 93023
coffee.note: In Meiners Oaks, on the west side of the valley toward Highway 150 and the lake. Opens at 6 on Saturday and is done by 1, so it's a morning stop. Sunday is in doubt. The shop's own page says 6 to 1 and two listings say closed, so call first: 805-646-7821. One listing shows outdoor seating; the shop's own page doesn't. Nothing on bike parking. Farmer and the Cook is on the same street.
coffee.hours_hint: 6 a.m. to 1 p.m. Saturday; weekdays from 5 or 6 a.m. (sources differ); Sunday unconfirmed, call first

coffee.name: Three Birds
coffee.note: Downtown, a block or so off Ojai Avenue on Signal Street. Opens at 7 and stays open until 4, so it's the one for after the ride. Reviewers on two listings describe a large outdoor seating area. The café's own site doesn't mention it, and nothing mentions bike parking.

restaurants.name: Jim & Rob's Fresh Grill
restaurants.note: After the ride: burritos, tacos, burgers and breakfast downtown, with outside seating on front and side patios. Open daily from 9 a.m., to 8:30 p.m. Sunday to Thursday and 9 p.m. Friday and Saturday (its own page, Nov 2026). The bar next door, Lisa's Cantina, is the same business, 11:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily. Cheap. (805) 640-1301.

restaurants.name: Farmer and the Cook
restaurants.address: 339 W El Roblar Dr, Ojai, CA 93023
restaurants.note: After the ride, on the west end in Meiners Oaks: an organic market and café with vegetarian and vegan Mexican food, a bakery, an espresso bar and a smoothie bar. Opens 8 a.m. every day; closes 4 p.m. Monday to Wednesday and 8 p.m. Thursday to Sunday, with pizza 5 to 8 p.m. Friday, Saturday and Sunday (its own page, Nov 2026). (805) 640-9608.

restaurants.name: Boccali's Pizza & Pasta
restaurants.note: The night before: pizza, lasagna and pasta on the East End, eaten on the patio or the oak-covered lawn. It's on East Ojai Avenue, the road the Upper Ojai climb goes out on. Open to 9 p.m. every night; from 11:45 a.m. Wednesday to Sunday, from 4 p.m. Monday and Tuesday (its own page, Nov 2026). Large groups email ahead; the lawn can be reserved. No pets. 805-646-6116.

restaurants.name: Papa Lennon's Pizzeria
restaurants.address: 515 W El Roblar Drive, Ojai, CA 93023
restaurants.note: The night before, for a group that didn't book: no reservations, order at the counter, seats up to 80, with a patio. Pizza, pasta and sandwiches, with gluten-free dough and pasta. In Meiners Oaks; the Channel Islands Bicycle Club picked it for lunch on its April 2026 Sulphur Mountain ride. Open daily 11:30 a.m. to 8 p.m. (its own page, Nov 2026), so eat early. (805) 640-7388.

restaurants.name: Ojai Deer Lodge
restaurants.note: A tavern on Maricopa Highway, the road the Highway 33 climb is on, with burgers, weekend barbecue, a large dog-friendly patio and live music. Closed Monday and Tuesday. Noon to 8 p.m. Wednesday and Thursday, noon to 9 Friday, 11 a.m. to 9 Saturday, 11 to 8 Sunday; the bar runs to midnight Friday and Saturday (its own page, Nov 2026). Parties of 12 or more ask ahead on the site. 805-646-4256.

restaurants.name: Radio Roma
restaurants.note: Late: a mezcal bar downtown that serves tacos and mariscos from the taqueria next door. Open 5 p.m. to midnight Thursday to Saturday, 5 to 11 p.m. Tuesday, Wednesday and Sunday, closed Monday (its own page, Nov 2026). A bar first and a small menu; the page doesn't say when the kitchen stops. (805) 272-8140.

restaurants.name: Ojai Rôtie
restaurants.note: The one to go back for: rotisserie chicken and sourdough downtown. Lunch 11:30 to 3:30 Wednesday to Sunday; dinner 4:30 to 8 Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, to 8:30 Friday and Saturday; closed Monday and Tuesday (its own page, Nov 2026). Reservations for four or more only. The Infatuation (Jan 2026) says it has a large front patio. (805) 798-9227.

hotels.name: Blue Iguana Inn
hotels.note: The one on the path. Its own page puts it "two miles from downtown Ojai" with "onsite bike rental" and "the adjacent Ojai Valley Trail." Rooms, suites and cottages around a pool. Its policies page says "Weekends require at least a 2-night booking" and that holidays and special events may need longer; check-in is 3 pm. Nothing about bringing your own bike. Check the site for rates.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: Ojai Rancho Inn
hotels.note: West end of town, about half a mile from the center, where Highway 33 comes in. 17 rooms, a pool and a bar on site. Its amenities list says "Complimentary bicycles for use" and the page calls town "an easy 5 minute bike ride," or 15 minutes on foot by the path behind the property. Free parking, fridge and microwave in the rooms. Nothing about bringing your own bike. Check the site for rates.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: Hummingbird Inn
hotels.note: East side, about a mile from the center on Ojai Avenue, on the way out to the orchard roads. Pool, fire pit, fridges and microwaves in the rooms. Its home page says "grab a complimentary bicycle and tour Ojai." Its rooms page says the patio rooms are downstairs. Ask for one if you have a bike. Nothing about bringing your own. $186 a night before tax on Hotels.com for Nov 17–18 (read Nov 15, 2026).
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: Casa Ojai Inn
hotels.note: East side on Ojai Avenue, the same stretch as the Hummingbird and across from Soule Park Golf Course. Its page says more about bikes than any other place to stay in town: "All guests at Casa Ojai and our sister hotel Su Nido Inn are welcome to use our complimentary bicycles," and the amenities list has "Bicycles, Locks, and Helmets included with amenity fee" plus a "hydration station available for refilling water bottles." Saltwater pool. The amenity fee isn't priced on the page (Nov 2026). Check the site for rates. The site's footer is dated 2022, so call before you count on it.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: The Oakridge Inn
hotels.address: 780 N. Ventura Ave, Oak View, CA 93022
hotels.note: The cheap one, down the valley in Oak View: "4 miles south of Ojai" and "2 miles east of Lake Casitas," by its own page, on Highway 33. A 33-room motel that prints its rates: one queen $109–$129 Sunday to Thursday and $139–$299 Friday and Saturday; two queens $119–$139 and $149–$299 (read Nov 15, 2026; the page says to call for holiday and event rates). Group discount for 10 rooms or more, not on major weekends. Nothing about bikes anywhere on the site.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: Ojai Valley Inn
hotels.note: The splurge: the big golf resort on the west side of town. Its activities page says "Pick up a complimentary Linus bicycle" and lists two guided bike tours, about 3 and about 7 miles. Those are cruisers for a picnic, not a ride. Nothing about bringing your own bike. Check the site for rates.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

bike_shops.name: The Mob Shop
bike_shops.note: Downtown Ojai, on Ojai Avenue. The one shop in town, with a workshop and a rental fleet. Monday, Thursday and Friday 10 to 5, Saturday 9 to 5, Sunday 9 to 4; closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Tune-ups from $99 (Basic) to $189 (Premium-Plus), wash and lube $39, 50-hour fork or shock service $95 plus parts, and wheelbuilding (Nov 2026). The page gives no turnaround time, so call before you count on a same-day fix. Rentals are book-ahead only, no walk-ins. The bikes: ENVE Melee road bike in 54, 56 and 58, ENVE MOG and Salsa Flyway gravel bikes, a Moots Vamoots 33 and Pivot mountain bikes. Prices show once you pick dates in the booking tool. Security deposit at pick-up, helmets included. The rental pages say these bikes "may not be rented for mass start events or races," so ask the shop before you plan one for an organized ride.

bike_shops.name: Ventura Bike Depot
bike_shops.note: Downtown Ventura, about 12 miles south of Ojai. The reason to make the trip: it's open every day, 9 to 5, so it covers the Tuesday and Wednesday when the Ojai shop is closed. Safety check $49, basic tune-up $89, standard tune-up $149, deluxe $299, parts extra (Nov 2026); e-bike work is mechanical only. Rents "premium road bikes" and hardtail mountain bikes by the block, from four hours to four days, plus Gazelle e-bikes. The page doesn't name the road bike models or sizes, so ask. Helmet free with a rental. A local shop since 1995, by its own About page.

bike_shops.name: Trek Bicycle Ventura
bike_shops.note: East Ventura, about 13 miles south of Ojai. The nearest shop that puts a turnaround in writing: service on any brand, no appointment needed, with "24-hour turnaround on most service jobs" and a free bike check. Level One $99.99, Level Two $189.99, Level Three from $449.99; boxes a bike to ship home for $79.99 (Nov 2026). Monday to Friday 11 to 6, Saturday 10 to 6, Sunday noon to 5. The page lists group rides and clinics but no schedule, and says nothing about receiving a shipped bike.

bike_shops.name: Ventura Bike HUB (Bike Ventura County)
bike_shops.note: Ventura's community bike shop, about 12 miles south of Ojai. Fix it yourself: stand time is $10 an hour with tools and a mechanic or volunteer to help (Nov 2026). Sells used bikes and the parts a traveler runs out of: tires, tubes, cables and housing, pedals, derailleurs. Wednesday and Thursday noon to 5, Friday 11 to 5, Saturday 10 to 5; closed Sunday to Tuesday. Bike Ventura County runs its community rides from here, {ride:ventura-ca-bikevc-brew-ride|the Brew Ride} among them.

culture.name: Bart's Books
culture.note: An outdoor bookstore: shelves in a courtyard, open to the sky. Its own page says it has served Ojai since 1964 and holds over 130,000 used and new books. Open every day 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., rain days included, closed Thanksgiving and Christmas (its site, Nov 2026); (805) 646-3755. An after-the-ride stop, not a before.

culture.name: Ojai Valley Brewery & Side Street Wine
culture.note: A small brewery and winery with a tasting room and a big outdoor patio. It's about five minutes from downtown by its own listing, on Bryant Street, the street the Ojai Valley Trail's Ojai end is on. Open Monday to Thursday 4 to 9 p.m., Friday 3 to 10, Saturday noon to 11, Sunday 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. (its Google listing, Nov 2026); (805) 798-9282. Weekends bring a food vendor and a band; the listing showed six such nights in September and October 2026. The patio is the room for a group.

culture.name: Ojai Certified Farmers' Market
culture.note: Sundays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., all year, rain or shine, behind the Arcade (Ventura County agricultural commissioner's market list; the market's LocalHarvest listing, updated Jan 2025). Produce, flowers and food from the growers. On Center Ride Out Sunday the riders roll by 7:00 am, so this one is for whoever drove up, and for any other weekend.

culture.name: Ojai Playhouse
culture.note: The town's one movie house, 200 seats, built in 1914. A flood shut it in 2014 and it reopened November 22, 2024 after a long rebuild. It runs 35mm and 4K film, plus comedy, talks and music, and has a café and a bar, by its own reopening release. Listings for the week of Nov 15, 2026 show films most days, afternoons and evenings. Check showtimes on its site.

culture.name: Ojai Valley Museum
culture.note: Valley history and local art in an old chapel on the main street: one gallery that changes about four times a year, a Sespe Wilderness diorama, a Chumash garden round the patio. Open Thursday to Sunday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., to 7 p.m. on third Fridays, when it's free. Suggested donation $5 (Nov 2026); (805) 640-1390. It was closed for remodeling in mid-November 2026; its page says normal hours resume Thursday, November 19. An hour, not an afternoon.

culture.name: Libbey Bowl
culture.note: The outdoor stage in the oak grove at the back of Libbey Park, downtown: 973 seats and a lawn for 200 to 300 more. Home of the Ojai Music Festival each June, a concert season and free community nights. No pets at shows, and one sealed water bottle a person. Its page lists nothing for April 2027 yet; check the calendar before the trip. Street parking nearby, free and metered.

clubs.name: Easy Rider (Channel Islands Bicycle Club and BikeVentura)
clubs.note: The closest thing to a group ride into the Ojai Valley. Free rides from the Museum of Ventura County lot, in two groups: Easy Rider and a longer Easy Rider Plus. The group calls them beginner-friendly and no-drop. Its Nov 15, 2026 ride sent the Plus group up the path to Meiners Oaks, about 29 miles round trip. Sign the online waiver first, and be able to ride 20 miles at 12 mph. Day and time: {ride:ventura-ca-easy-rider-community-ride|the Easy Rider ride}.

clubs.name: Channel Islands Bicycle Club
clubs.note: A road club in Ventura that describes itself as social riding. Weekly rides leave from Ventura, and special rides come up to Ojai. It posted a Sulphur Mountain gravel and road loop into Ojai for April 2, 2026: 47 miles from the Museum lot or 32 from the Sulphur Mountain trailhead, with lunch in Meiners Oaks. Ride as a member, or sign the ride waiver on the club's calendar page.

clubs.name: Great Outdoors — Santa Barbara Ventura County chapter
clubs.note: An all-volunteer LGBTQIA+ and allies outdoors club, not a cycling club. It hikes and camps. It has led a bike ride from Ventura up the trail to Ojai and back: 30 miles at a pace it called leisurely, with lunch in downtown Ojai (Nov 23, 2025). No bike ride was on its calendar on Nov 15, 2026, so check the outings page. Register for an outing on the site. Membership is $25 a year (Nov 2026).

bring_your_bike.summary: Bring it, and plan on a car. Ojai has no airport. Santa Barbara is about 34 miles west in a straight line, Burbank about 54 and Los Angeles International about 59 southeast. No airport page names a shuttle to town. Delta, American and Southwest all check a packed bike at the standard bag fee (Nov 2026), so flying with it costs less than renting. The Mob Shop downtown rents road, gravel and mountain bikes by advance booking only. It's closed Tuesday and Wednesday, and it says its performance bikes can't be rented for mass-start events or races. No shop in the Ojai Valley or Ventura says on its own site that it receives a shipped bike. Once you're in town with a built bike, you can ride to everything.

airports.name: Santa Barbara Airport
airports.note: The closest airport with airline service, about 34 miles west in a straight line; the drive is longer. Alaska (Portland, San Diego, Seattle), American (Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix), Delta (Salt Lake City), Southwest (Las Vegas, Oakland, Sacramento, Denver, San Diego) and United (Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, San Francisco) (the airport's airlines page, last modified Sept 29, 2026). Uber and Lyft pick up in front of the terminal; taxis, rental cars and the Santa Barbara Airbus are listed on the airport's ground-transport page. That page says nothing about oversized bags and names no service to Ojai. 500 James Fowler Road, Santa Barbara.

airports.name: Hollywood Burbank
airports.note: About 54 miles southeast in a straight line. Alaska, Allegiant, American, Breeze, Delta, JetBlue, Southwest and United (the airport's FAQ, Nov 2026). Ten rental car companies on site in one building, and an Amtrak and Metrolink station on Empire Avenue. The easier Los Angeles airport to get a rental car and a bike case out of. 2827 N Hollywood Way, Burbank.

airports.name: Los Angeles International
airports.note: About 59 miles southeast in a straight line; the most flights. Alaska, Southwest, Delta, American and United (the airport's airline list, Sept 2026). Ride apps and taxis pick up at the LAX-it lot; rental car offices are off airport by shuttle (Sept 2026). The Ojai Valley Inn's directions page has you on the 101 for about 50 miles, then Highway 33 for 14 more (Nov 2026).

fly.airline_note: From each airline's own page, Nov 2026, unless marked. Delta: a non-motorized touring or single-seat racing bike in a container built for bikes goes at the standard bag allowance and fee; over 50 lb pays the excess weight fee; 100 lb or more, or over 115 linear inches, is refused; a hard-shell bike case needs no release form, a soft bag signs a limited release; some Delta Connection flights exclude bikes. First bag $45, second $55, US domestic Main Cabin. American: one non-motorized touring, mountain, tandem or racing bike in a hard case, a bike bag or a box built for bikes; standard checked bag fee up to 50 lb, standard overweight fee from 50 to 70 lb, oversize fees do not apply; handlebars sideways, pedals off or wrapped; not in a hard case it is treated as fragile. Main Cabin first bag $50 at the airport or $45 online, second $60 or $55, for tickets issued on or after April 9, 2026; overweight is $30 for 50 to 53 lb and $100 for 53 to 70 lb. Southwest: a non-motorized single-seat bike is checked baggage at standard checked bag and overweight fees, oversize fees waived; over 100 lb or 115 inches is refused; pedals and handlebars removed and wrapped; cardboard or a soft case flies with a limited release. The Southwest bike page gives no dollar figures, so read its fee page. Alaska (Sept 2026): a cased bike is a standard checked bag, oversize waived and overweight waived to 70 lb, first bag $45, second $55. United: we don't have its rule, so read its sports-equipment page before you book. Keep the case under 50 lb and it's one ordinary checked bag on every carrier above but United.

ship.note: No shop in the Ojai Valley or Ventura says on its own site that it receives and builds a shipped bike (Nov 15, 2026). The Mob Shop's contact, workshop and store-policy pages say nothing about shipping, boxing or assembly; call (805) 272-8102 before you send anything. It's closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Trek Bicycle Ventura boxes a bike for the trip home for $79.99 (Nov 2026). That covers leaving, not arriving. The carriers people use (Sept 2026): BikeFlights ships by UPS, states no transit-day count and says to allow an extra day or two for weather; ShipBikes, also UPS ground, says no more than 6 business days one way in the continental US. If a shop agrees to take it, ship at least a week ahead.

rent.note: One rental shop in Ojai: The Mob Shop, downtown. Book ahead; it takes no walk-ins. Its rental pages say the performance bikes "may not be rented for mass start events or races" and can't be transported without the shop's permission. So it suits a ride from town, or the people who drove up to meet a Center Ride Out rider. Ask the shop before you plan one for an organized ride. Ventura Bike Depot, about 12 miles south, rents road bikes and is open every day. The math: a bike case is a standard checked bag on Delta, American and Southwest, about $90 round trip on Delta or American paid online (Nov 2026). For a fit you depend on, or a visit that covers a Tuesday or Wednesday, bring yours.

shops.name: The Mob Shop
shops.note: Downtown Ojai. ENVE Melee road bike (54 fits 5'8" to 5'11", 56 fits 5'10" to 6'1", 58 fits 6'0" to 6'3"); ENVE MOG gravel (54); Salsa Flyway carbon gravel (Small 5'2" to 5'6", Large 5'11" to 6'3"); Moots Vamoots 33; Pivot mountain bikes. Electric and town bikes too. Prices show once you pick dates. Book in advance, security deposit at pick-up, helmets provided. Full refund more than 24 hours out, half inside 24. Not for mass-start events or races; no transporting the bike without the shop's permission. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

shops.name: Ventura Bike Depot
shops.note: Downtown Ventura, about 12 miles south. "Premium road bikes" and hardtail mountain bikes with hydraulic discs and a dropper post, rented from four hours to four days; rates on the page run from $65 to $245 (Nov 2026). Models and sizes aren't listed, so call. Open daily 9 to 5.

get_around.note: To get here with a bike case, yes. Ojai has no airport and no train. The nearest airline airport is Santa Barbara, about 34 miles west in a straight line; Burbank and Los Angeles International are about 54 and 59 southeast. Neither the Santa Barbara nor the Burbank ground-transport page names a shuttle to Ojai, and a bus rack takes a built bike, not a box. Rent a car at the airport, or book a large rideshare and expect the case to ride in the back. From Santa Barbara the Ojai Valley Inn's directions page gives two ways off the 101: Highway 33 from Ventura, 14 miles to town, or Route 150 over Casitas Pass, which it advises against in rain, at night or if you don't know the road (Nov 2026). Once you're in Ojai with a built bike you don't need the car. The town is 4.4 square miles, the one bike shop is downtown, and the bike path runs about 15 miles down the valley to Ventura (VCTC's bike booklet). Center Ride Out riders arrive on the bike; this is for the people driving up to meet them.
get_around.transit_bike_rules: Gold Coast Transit Route 16 links downtown Ojai (the City lists stops at the Y, Blanche, Signal and the Park n' Ride) with the Ventura Transit Center at Pacific View Mall (Ojai transit audit, April 2026). Gold Coast's bike page (Nov 2026): every fixed-route bus has a front rack for three bikes, first come, first served; the bike rides free; tell the driver before you load, and load from the curb side. E-bikes that don't fold go on the rack; batteries must be sealed lithium-ion; no gas-powered or homemade bikes. A folded bike can come aboard if it is secured and out of the aisle. The page gives no size or weight limit, and the district takes no responsibility for damage. The Ojai Trolley is the City's own bus: one route along Ojai Avenue and Maricopa Highway, out to Meiners Oaks and Mira Monte, about hourly, weekdays roughly 6:30 am to 7:30 pm and weekends roughly 7 am to 8 pm, every day but seven holidays (audit, April 2026; the City's page). $1.50 a ride or $4 a day, exact fare, free with a transfer from Gold Coast (effective Jan 1, 2026). Nothing the City publishes says whether the trolley carries bikes; ask at (805) 646-5581 ext. 207. The nearest train is the Pacific Surfliner in Ventura, about 12 miles south in a straight line: a full-size bike rides free with a reserved bike space, up to 50 lb and 4-inch tires, standard e-bikes included (Pacific Surfliner's bike page, Nov 2026).

bike_share.note: No bike share was found in Ojai (Nov 2026). Rent from the shop, or stay at one of the inns that lend bikes.

bring_your_bike.rules_and_safety: California law (Nov 2026). Drivers must give three feet when passing a bike (Vehicle Code 21760); where a second lane runs the same way, the driver moves into it to pass if that is practicable; where three feet is not possible, the driver slows to a reasonable speed and passes only when it does not endanger the rider. The fine is $35, or $220 if a collision injures the rider (statute, Nov 11, 2026). Helmets are required under 18 (21212). E-bikes come in three classes (312.5): class 1 pedal-assist to 20 mph, class 2 throttle to 20 mph, class 3 pedal-assist to 28 mph with a speedometer, rider 16 or older and helmeted. Ride as far right as practicable except when passing, turning left, avoiding a hazard or in a lane too narrow to share (21202). No earbuds in both ears (27400). At night, a white headlight and a red rear reflector or light (21201). Sidewalk riding is set city by city (21206); we couldn't find Ojai's own rule, so walk the bike under the Arcade. CalBike's page (modified Aug 24, 2026) does not list a stop-as-yield law; a rider may go on the walk signal (21456). On the Ojai Valley Trail, class 1 and class 2 e-bikes are allowed; class 3 is not allowed on shared-use paths unless a local ordinance says so (VCTC's bike booklet, undated). The read: the valley floor and the trail are the quiet miles, and the state highways out of town are mountain roads. The Ojai Valley Inn's own directions page tells drivers to skip Route 150 over Casitas Pass in rain, at night or if they don't know it (Nov 2026). A rider was killed on Cuyama Road near Del Norte Road in Ojai on Aug 7, 2020, on what BikinginLA, citing the Ojai Valley News, called a narrow two-lane country road with no shoulders. On Highway 33 north of town, Caltrans is rebuilding three tunnels near Wheeler Gorge (post miles 18.2 to 19.0). It shut the road to everyone for 55 hours on Aug 28 to 31, 2026, and expects to finish in winter 2026/2027 (Caltrans release, Aug 12, 2026). Check Caltrans before you plan that climb.

faq.q: Which Ojai hotels have complimentary bikes for guests?
faq.a: Four say so on their own pages. Ojai Rancho Inn lists "Complimentary bicycles for use," Hummingbird Inn says "grab a complimentary bicycle and tour Ojai," Casa Ojai Inn lists "Bicycles, Locks, and Helmets included with amenity fee," and Ojai Valley Inn says "Pick up a complimentary Linus bicycle." None of them states a policy on bringing your own bike into the room, so ask when you book.

faq.q: What coffee shop in Ojai opens at 6 a.m.?
faq.a: Ojai Coffee Roasters, downtown at 337 E. Ojai Ave., opens at 6 a.m. every day, Saturday and Sunday included; its kitchen runs 9 to 2. Coffee Connection in Meiners Oaks opens at 6 on Saturday and closes at 1, but its Sunday hours aren't settled, so call first.

faq.q: Where can I rent a road bike in Ojai?
faq.a: The Mob Shop, 110 W Ojai Ave. It rents an ENVE Melee road bike in 54, 56 and 58, plus gravel and mountain bikes, by advance booking only, with no walk-ins, and it's closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Its rental pages say these bikes "may not be rented for mass start events or races," so ask the shop before you plan one for an organized ride.

faq.q: How long is the Ojai Valley Trail, and is it paved?
faq.a: It's 9.3 miles and paved, a car-free rail-trail from Bryant Street in Ojai to Foster Park. There it meets the Ventura River Trail, which makes about 15 miles one way from Ojai to Ventura. Some stretches are bumpy and cracked from tree roots, and it gets crowded on weekends.

faq.q: Should I bring my bike to Ojai?
faq.a: Yes, and plan on a car, because Ojai has no airport and no train. Delta, American and Southwest check a packed bike at the standard bag fee (Nov 2026), and Ojai's one rental shop is book-ahead only and closed Tuesday and Wednesday. No shop in the Ojai Valley or Ventura says it receives a shipped bike.

faq.q: Where do Center Ride Out riders sleep in Ojai?
faq.a: They camp. The ride reaches Ojai on Friday, April 23, 2027 and rolls for Los Angeles by 7:00 am on Sunday, and the Center has not published where the camp is. The hotels in this guide are for whoever drives up to meet a rider.
